arte.universo: Ancient China about 2,000 years ago (a dim wooden counting room with paper lanterns, abacus-free tables covered with thin bamboo counting rods, some painted red and some black, silk scrolls and ink brushes); India in the 7th century (a stone astronomer's study with carved columns, oil lamps, palm-leaf manuscripts tied with string, a brass astrolabe, night sky with stars through an arched window); Europe in the 1500s to 1700s (a candlelit scholar's library with heavy books, quills and printed pages); and modern Mexico on a cold early morning. No portraits and no recognizable real people: the mathematicians are never shown, only their objects and places. Anonymous people only from behind or far away. No readable writing, letters or digits anywhere.

escena.accion: In a vast dark space, a long line of small glowing dots runs from the center to the right like a path of lights; to the left of a single bright central dot there is only darkness and empty void. The Pasita stands at the bright central dot looking toward the dark empty left side

escena.objeto: A horizontal path of glowing lime-green light dots going only to the right, ending at a bright center point; nothing on the left (no digits, no symbols)
escena.foreground: Soft dark mist on the ground, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The Pasita on the bright central dot
escena.background: Deep dark void, faint stars only on the right side
escena.iluminacion: Lime glow from the dots on the right, cold darkness on the left

escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, three-quarter view, backpack on, one hand touching the palm leaves, thoughtful

cuerpo: De ahí viene **menos por menos da más**.
En 1758 aún había quien decía que **no existían**.

escena.accion: In a candlelit 18th-century European library, the Pasita stands on a wooden chair beside a big desk with a pile of heavy closed leather books and one open book with blank pages, frowning in disbelief
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, three-quarter view, backpack on, arms crossed, skeptical
escena.objeto: A pile of heavy leather-bound books and one open book with blank pages, a quill in an ink pot
escena.foreground: A brass candlestick with a melting candle, slightly blurred
escena.background: Tall dark bookshelves fading into shadow, a tall window with rain
escena.iluminacion: Single warm candle against cold blue darkness
escena.composicion: Medium shot; the upper 42% is the dark shelves and ceiling

cuerpo: En tu saldo, en el frío, en el **sótano −1**.

escena.accion: On a very cold early morning in a Mexican city, the Pasita waits at a bus stop with a scarf, her breath making a little cloud of vapor; frost covers the grass and the windows of parked cars
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, three-quarter view, backpack on, wearing a knitted scarf, hands in front of her mouth to warm them
escena.objeto: Frost on the grass and a white cloud of breath

escena.midground: The Pasita at the bus stop

escena.emocion: Everyday life: the math is everywhere

post:
Durante siglos, los números negativos se consideraban absurdos. 🔢

En China, hace unos 2,000 años, ya se contaba con varitas: rojas para lo que se tiene y negras para lo que se debe (al revés de nuestros "números rojos"). En el año 628, el matemático indio Brahmagupta les puso reglas y los llamó fortunas y deudas: "deuda por deuda da fortuna", o sea, menos por menos da más.

Europa tardó siglos en aceptarlos: en 1758, el matemático Francis Maseres todavía decía que no existían. Hoy los ves en tu saldo, en el termómetro y en el botón del sótano.

¿Dónde viste un número negativo hoy? 👇
